en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 15.1.
Hetuduka, Kusalattika (The Dyad on Roots, the Triad on the Wholesome)
15.1.1. Section on the Wholesome (Kusalapada) Homage to the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Dependent upon a root wholesome state, a non-root non-wholesome state arises by way of the root condition. Dependent upon a non-root...
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not a root, a state that is neither a root nor wholesome arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both a root and wholesome, and a state that is not a root but wholesome, a state that is neither a root nor wholesome arises by way of root-condition.
… Three [cases] (these concern only mind-originated [matter]; there is no object-condition).
With respect to root-condition, there are three; with respect to predominance-condition, there are three ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance-condition, there are three.
(The "Conascent" section ... pe ... and the "Supported" section are the same as the "Dependent" section.
A wholesome state that is a root-condition is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither a root nor wholesome.
A wholesome state that is a root-condition (*hetu*) is related to a state that is neither a root-condition nor wholesome by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*) ... three.
A wholesome state that is not a root-condition is related to a state that is neither a root-condition nor wholesome by way of object-condition ... three.
Wholesome states that are both root-conditions and not root-conditions are related to a state that is neither a root-condition nor wholesome by way of object-condition ... three. (Abbreviated.)
In the cause condition, one; in the object condition, nine; in the predominance condition, nine; in the proximity and contiguity conditions, nine;
in the conascence and dependence conditions, three; in the strong-dependence condition, nine; in the postnascence condition, three; in the kamma condition, one; in the nutriment condition, one;

in the faculty condition, three; in the jhāna condition, one; in the path condition, three; in the dissociation condition, three ... [and so on] ... in the non-disappearance condition, three. (The "Chapter of Questions" should also be expanded in detail.)
15.1.2. Unwholesome Section (Akusalapada) Dependent on a root unwholesome state, a non-root non-unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a non-root unwholesome state, a non-root non-unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a root unwholesome state and a non-root unwholesome state, a non-root non-unwholesome state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; under predominance [condition] there are three ... pe ...
under non-disappearance [condition] there are three. (The "Conascent Chapter" ... pe ... and the "Supported Chapter" are the same as the "Dependent Chapter.
A root unwholesome state is a condition, by way of root condition, for a non-root non-unwholesome state.
A root unwholesome state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-root non-unwholesome state … three.
A non-root unwholesome state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-non-root non-unwholesome state … three.
Both a root unwholesome state and a non-root unwholesome state are conditions, by way of object-condition, for a non-root non-unwholesome state … three. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to root: one; with respect to object: nine; with respect to predominance: one; with respect to proximity and contiguity: nine;
with respect to conascence and dependence: three; with respect to strong-dependence: nine; with respect to postnascence: three; with respect to kamma: one;

with respect to nutriment: one; with respect to faculty: three; with respect to jhāna: one; with respect to path: three; with respect to dissociation: three ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance: three.

15.1.3. Unexplained Section on Non-Root (Abyākatapada Nahetu) Dependent on a non-root unexplained state, there arises a non-root non-unexplained state by way of root condition. There are three [answers] under root; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance. (The section on dependence and the section on inquiry should also be expanded in detail.)
